main_text.l: VIII. Nimia & immoderata studia. Hic
vero est hostis omnium deterrimus. Nimirum ingenii
vigor & acrimonia atteritur, exhauritur nimiis vi-
giliis. Nam spiritus vitales in corde, & animales in
cerebro fatigantur nimium quantum vigiliis & stu-
diis. Immane quantum est facinus corporis proprii
esse carnificem! Immoderatis vigiliis ac praepropero
IX. Mutatio præceptorum. Videte mihi eti-
am hunc hostem, ordine quidem postremum, sed vi
facile principem. Præcepta mutare, præceptores mu-
tare, id vero egregie facit ad eruditionis cornucopiæ
comparandum. Scilicet. Hodie quid crebrius! Is, ut
monet majorum gentium Orator, qui cupit in aliquo
excellere, unius ingenio familiariter applicare se de-
bet. Oportet igitur certis præceptis veluti innutriri,
oportet ad pedes alicujus præceptoris eum perdiu edu-
cari & edoceri, qui cupit fundamenta jacere.
Atq; hæc sunt illa impedimenta, per quæ fiat, quo
minus hodie maxima studiosorum pars pro-
grediatur, quodq; in medio etiam
cursu deficiant.

page.notes: Printed "Cap.5." at the lower right is treated as the catchword. The Greek word after "illud" is uncertain: it is read as πολυδρύλλιον but the scan is not clear. "HOCAGES;" is printed with letter spacing and is underlined. The strikethrough over "non concoquunt" and the underlines in the text are not reproduced as markup. The "q;" abbreviations in "Atq;" and "quodq;" are read from a small mark and may be wrong. The note marker for the IX note is a short bracket mark, and the note is transcribed as printed. The phrase "vi-giliis" keeps the printed hyphen.
